description: The 'commits_cached' dataset provides a detailed record of software development activities, specifically focusing on commit data. This dataset is particularly useful for analyzing the history and evolution of a software project by examining individual commits. Each entry in the dataset represents a single commit, identified by a unique commit ID, and includes information about the project it belongs to, the author of the commit, and the timestamp of when the commit was made. Additionally, the dataset captures the number of files and lines added, removed, or changed in each commit, offering insights into the scale and impact of changes. This dataset can be used by software developers, project managers, and researchers to track project progress, identify trends in development practices, and assess the contributions of different team members. It is also valuable for automated tools that analyze code changes for quality assurance or to predict future development needs.
shortDesc: Dataset of cached commit data with project, author, and file changes.

columns.name: project_key
columns.comment: Unique identifier for the project, key for project tracking.

columns.name: commit_id
columns.comment: Unique identifier for each commit, essential for version control.

columns.name: author
columns.comment: Name of the person who made the commit, tracks contributions.

columns.name: timestamp
columns.comment: Time when the commit was made, crucial for chronological analysis.

columns.name: added_files
columns.comment: Number of files added in the commit, indicates new additions.

columns.name: added_lines
columns.comment: Number of lines added in the commit, measures code growth.

columns.name: removed_files
columns.comment: Number of files removed in the commit, shows deletions.

columns.name: removed_lines
columns.comment: Number of lines removed in the commit, indicates code reduction.

columns.name: changed_files
columns.comment: Number of files changed in the commit, reflects modifications.
